questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties?

1) The 44th amendment Act introduced Fundamental duties in the Constitution.

2) Fundamental Duties were expanded by the 86th amendment act.

3) Article 51A (a) entails respect its ideals and institutions, national flag and the national anthem.

4) Fundamental Duty obliges parents to provide opportunities for education to their child between 6-14 years of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the Fundamental Duties were introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, not the 44th Amendment Act.
 
• **Option 2** is correct. The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, expanded the Fundamental Duties to include the duty of parents to provide opportunities for education to their children between the ages of 6 and 14.
 
• **Option 3** is correct. Article 51A (a) entails respecting the ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• **Option 4** is correct. The Fundamental Duty obliges parents to provide opportunities for education to their child between 6-14 years of age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IVA of the Constitution of India under Article 51A.
 
• They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were listed, and the 86th Amendment Act added an 11th duty.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.

questions.question: What is the name of the scheme aimed at conservation of wetlands, which was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrit Dharohar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amrit Dharohar** is the name of the scheme aimed at the conservation of wetlands, which was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24.
 
• The scheme is designed to enhance the protection and management of wetlands across India.
 
• Wetlands are crucial ecosystems that support a wide range of biodiversity and provide numerous environmental benefits such as water filtration, flood control, and carbon sequestration.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's broader efforts to promote sustainable development and environmental conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil all year or for varying periods during the year, including during the growing season.
 
• India is a signatory to the Ramsar Convention, an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.
 
• The Ramsar Convention aims to halt the worldwide loss of wetlands and to conserve, through wise use and management, those that remain.
 
• India has 94 Ramsar sites, covering an area of over 1.3 million hectares.
 
• Conserving wetlands can also help in achieving several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including those related to water, climate action, and life on land.

questions.question: Which of the following occupies less memory when saving an MS-Word file?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**docx**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **docx** files typically occupy less memory compared to other MS-Word file formats.
 
• The **docx** format is a compressed file format, which makes it more storage-efficient.
 
• Introduced in Microsoft Word 2007, **docx** is an XML-based file format that reduces file size and improves data recovery options.
 
• In contrast, **doc** files, which were used in versions of Microsoft Word prior to 2007, are generally larger because they are not compressed.
 
• The **docm** format is similar to **docx** but includes macros, which can increase the file size.
 
• The **docc** format is not a standard MS-Word file format.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using the **docx** format can improve file-sharing and storage efficiency.
 
• It also supports a variety of advanced features such as improved graphics and better integration with other Microsoft Office applications.
 
• Due to its widespread adoption, **docx** files are highly compatible with various word processing software.
 
• Converting older **doc** files to **docx** can help in saving storage space.

questions.question: Which is the natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir Forest**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gir Forest** is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in India.
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, the Gir Forest National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is home to the last remaining population of Asiatic Lions.
 
• The Asiatic Lion, also known as **Panthera leo persica**, once roamed from the Middle East to India, but now they are confined to this single location due to habitat loss and hunting.
 
• Conservation efforts in the Gir Forest have been crucial in increasing the population of these lions from the brink of extinction.
 
• The Gir Forest covers an area of approximately **1,412 square kilometers** and comprises diverse flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Gir National Park** was established in 1965 and has since been a protected area for wildlife conservation.
 
• The Government of Gujarat and various wildlife organizations have implemented several measures to protect and increase the population of Asiatic Lions.
 
• Tourism in the Gir Forest is regulated to ensure minimal disturbance to the wildlife and their natural habitat.
 
• The Asiatic Lion differs from its African counterpart by being slightly smaller with a less developed mane.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to explore potential sites for reintroducing the Asiatic Lion to reduce the risk of the entire population being confined to a single area.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding invertebrates from the options given below.

options.text: They possess a backbone and an internal skeleton.
They have radial or bilateral body symmetry.
They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
They have open circulatory system as there is no organisation in the distribution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They possess a backbone and an internal skeleton**__

__
 
• Invertebrates do not possess a backbone or an internal skeleton.
 
• They exhibit either radial or bilateral body symmetry.
 
• They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
 
• They typically have an open circulatory system as there is no organization in the distribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Invertebrates constitute a vast majority of animal species on Earth, covering groups such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and more.
 
• Despite lacking a backbone, many invertebrates have specialized adaptations that allow them to thrive in diverse environments.
 
• The study of invertebrates is crucial for understanding ecological interactions, evolutionary biology, and the development of medical and technological innovations.
 
• Invertebrates play key roles in ecosystems, including pollination, decomposition, and serving as food for other animals.

questions.question: Which Governor General of India issued the famous Regulation XVII in 1829, which declared the practice of Sati illegal and punishable by the courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord William Bentinck** was the Governor General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• He issued the famous **Regulation XVII in 1829**, which declared the practice of Sati illegal and punishable by the courts.
 
• Regulation XVII was a significant step towards social reform in India, aiming to abolish the inhumane practice of Sati, where a widow was compelled to self-immolate on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• This regulation was a result of persistent efforts by social reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who campaigned against the practice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord William Bentinck** is also known for various other reforms, including the suppression of Thuggee and the introduction of English education in India.
 
• His tenure marked the beginning of several progressive changes in the Indian administrative system.
 
• The abolition of Sati was a landmark decision that highlighted the British administration's commitment to social reform and the protection of human rights.
 
• Regulation XVII faced opposition from orthodox sections of society, but it was upheld and enforced rigorously.
 
• Lord William Bentinck's efforts in abolishing Sati were later recognized as a pivotal moment in the history of Indian social reform.

questions.question: Secularism is a feature of the Indian Constitution, which means:

options.text: The State promotes the religion of the majority community.
The State does not promote any religion.
The State can promote any religion.
The State promotes the religion of the minority community.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The State does not promote any religion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secularism** in the Indian Constitution means that the State does not promote any religion.
 
• This ensures that there is no official state religion and that all religions are treated equally by the state.
 
• It is a fundamental aspect that protects the rights of individuals to practice and propagate their religion without any state interference.
 
• Secularism helps in maintaining the principle of separation of religion from the state, thus ensuring that religious groups do not interfere in government affairs and the government does not interfere in religious affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of **secularism** is enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, which declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.
 
• The Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of religion to all its citizens under **Articles 25 to 28**.
 
• Article 25 provides for freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• Article 26 ensures freedom to manage religious affairs.
 
• Article 27 ensures that no person shall be compelled to pay any taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 allows educational institutions maintained by the state to impart religious instruction.

• **Bharat Muni**, in his *Natya Shastra*, categorizes musical instruments based on the **different sounds** they produce.
 
• The categorization includes **four types of instruments**: stringed instruments (Tata), percussion instruments (Avanaddha), wind instruments (Sushira), and solid instruments (Ghana).
 
• This classification reflects the diverse ways in which sound can be produced in musical instruments.
 
• The *Natya Shastra* is an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The *Natya Shastra* is attributed to **Bharata Muni** and is believed to have been composed between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• It is a comprehensive guide to the **theory and practice** of the performing arts in ancient India.
 
• The text is considered the foundation of Indian classical music and dance traditions.
 
• It includes detailed instructions on the techniques of **acting, stage design, music, dance, and makeup**.
 
• The *Natya Shastra* has had a profound influence on the cultural and artistic traditions of India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the official language of Tripura?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kokborak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kokborak** is the official language of Tripura.
 
• It is one of the languages spoken by the Tripuri people in the Indian state of Tripura.
 
• Kokborak is also known as Tripuri or Tipra and is a Tibeto-Burman language.
 
• The language has its own script known as the "Koloma" script, although the Bengali script is also widely used.
 
• Efforts have been made to promote and preserve Kokborak through educational programs and cultural initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tripura** is a state in northeastern India, bordered by Bangladesh to the north, south, and west, and the Indian states of Assam and Mizoram to the east.
 
• The state has a rich cultural heritage with various indigenous communities, each having its own distinct language and traditions.
 
• In addition to Kokborak, Bengali is also widely spoken and understood in Tripura.
 
• Tripura became a full-fledged state of India on January 21, 1972.
 
• The state is known for its scenic beauty, diverse culture, and historical significance, including palaces, temples, and wildlife sanctuaries.

__
 
• **Ajit Kumar Mohanty** took over the charge of Chairman, **Atomic Energy Commission** in May 2023.
 
• The Atomic Energy Commission is responsible for the administration of the Atomic Energy Act, 1962, and it oversees the development and implementation of policies related to atomic energy in India.
 
• It plays a critical role in the planning and execution of nuclear power projects and research in the field of nuclear science and technology.
 
• The commission ensures the safe and secure use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, such as power generation, medical applications, and scientific research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Atomic Energy Commission** was established in 1948 to spearhead India's nuclear program.
 
• It functions under the Department of Atomic Energy, which is directly under the Prime Minister of India.
 
• The commission has been instrumental in the establishment of several nuclear power plants and research facilities across the country.
 
• It also collaborates with international organizations to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and to ensure adherence to global safety standards.
 
• India is committed to using nuclear energy as a means to achieve energy security and to reduce carbon emissions in line with its climate goals.
